name: Iraq
summary: Iraq, Day 199 — upgraded from bystander. Iranian-aligned militia territory (Maysan) was the confirmed launch origin of the 10-Sep drones that shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline; Baghdad condemned, sacked the local commander and closed then reopened the Shalamcheh crossing. Iraq simultaneously enjoys Iranian transit permits for its tankers (patronage) and suffers strikes in its waters (New Andros). Riyadh's restraint is explicitly conditional on Iraqi action — Iraq is the hinge on whether the Saudi–Iran confrontation goes direct.

recent_signals.headline: **No second Iraq-origin attack on Gulf energy (33 days); Saudi still not striking inside Iraq.** Kurdish/Iraqi faction sources: the 10-Sep pipeline drones came from a small network outside the Islamic Resistance answering to a senior IRGC commander — CLAIMED. Reuters (1 Oct): Tehran told allies in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq to prepare a coordinated response if US strikes resume — REPORTED. Iraq is one of three US–Iran message channels (Rezaei, 11 Oct). Iraqi exports ~2.6 mb/d to 21 Sep; Iraqi Oil Tankers Co. sent its own VLCC through Hormuz (~3 Oct). Drones struck the KDPI's Azadi camp at Koya, Erbil (12 Oct; no claim). Kata'ib Hezbollah praised the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia. — absence REPORTED.

**No second Iraq-origin attack on Saudi Arabia and no Saudi strike in Iraq 17–21 Sep.** Attribution housekeeping: Kpler's 17-Sep note calls the 10-Sep pumping-station strikes 'Houthi'; Riyadh and Baghdad place the launch in Maysan (commander dismissed 13 Sep, no claimant) — the graph follows the governments. — no-event CONFIRMED.

**Investigation into the 10–11 Sep East-West pipeline attack continues; no perpetrator named; Saudi restraint holds a 5th day.** Baghdad had confirmed the Maysan launch origin and sacked the provincial commander (12 Sep). Suspicion (FDD, a hawkish DC think tank; JPost analysis concurs) falls on the Badr Organization and Harakat Ansar Allah al-Awfiya (US-sanctioned); FDD notes the line that operatives acted 'without orders' would shield the parent militia from accountability. Separately, strikes attributed to IRAN by the Kurdish security agency (Tehran silent) hit Iraqi Kurdistan: five missiles at 03:10 on 14 Sep into Sulaimani province (three at the Komala families' camp at Zirgwez, one near Gurgachya, one in Qaradagh — no casualties; Asayish/Rudaw/IranWire) and a drone on a KDPI base at Balisan on 15 Sep (material damage). Komala ties the strikes to regime 'anxiety' ahead of the 16-Sep Mahsa Amini anniversary strike. Iraq is now both a launch pad against Saudi Arabia and a target of Iran. (FDD 16 Sep; Rudaw; IranWire; Hatha Alyoum) — CONFIRMED (strikes occurred, 3 sources) / ATTRIBUTED (Iranian origin — Asayish/Komala; no Iranian comment) / REPORTED (militia attribution).

**Iraq is now a launch pad, a patronage client and a victim at once.** Saudi says the drones that shut the East-West pipeline (10 Sep) came from Iraq; Baghdad traced them to Maysan, condemned the attack, dismissed the Maysan commander and briefly closed the Shalamcheh crossing with Iran (reopened by 13 Sep); no group claimed it; Trump: Iran 'probably responsible' (Al Jazeera, AP, Reuters — CONFIRMED origin; attribution to Iran REPORTED/CLAIMED). Earlier: Iranian drones reportedly targeted the KRG PM's office after reports the Kurds mediated Trump talks (17 Aug; Iran 'false flag'); Iraq secured Iranian Hormuz transit permits for its tankers (22 Aug); the Panama-flagged New Andros was drone-struck in Iraqi waters (9 Sep). Saudi is holding off retaliation 'at the Iraqi PM's request'.

**IRAQ JOINT PROBE OF THE MAY 17 SAUDI-AIRSPACE + UAE BARAKAH DRONE STRIKES — DAY 9 OF 14, NOTHING MATERIALLY NEW. UAE MAINTAINS ALL THREE BARAKAH DRONES TRACED TO IRAQI TERRITORY; IRAQ'S FM SAYS ITS AIR DEFENCES 'HAD NOT DETECTED' THEM; NO GROUP HAS CLAIMED; NO PUBLISHED FINDINGS.** Iraq's national security council under PM Ali Al-Zaidi continues the joint investigation with Saudi/UAE cooperation; Iran has not publicly acknowledged or denied any role and PMF militias have not publicly claimed attribution — consistent with the deniable-harassment ceiling [CONFIRMED — committee operating, no findings yet]. The Saudi formal kinetic response trigger (Day 9 of 14, by 2026-05-31) and UAE Barakah follow-on trigger (Day 8 of 14) both stay `watching` — channelled through this investigative track, not direct retaliation. Al-Zaidi's alignment 'with Trump's goal of limiting Iran's influence in the OPEC nation' (Bloomberg May 21) carries forward.
sources: The National (UAE) / Arab News / Euronews May 19-20
Shafaq News (Iraq air defences 'had not detected')

recent_signals.headline: **SAUDI FORMAL KINETIC RESPONSE TO IRAQI-AIRSPACE DRONES — DAY 3 OF 14 NEGATIVE-SPACE; NO IRAQI GOVERNMENT PUBLIC CLAIM OR DISCLAIMER ON DRONE LAUNCHES.** Iraqi government has not surfaced public attribution either claiming or disclaiming; PMU / Kata'ib Hezbollah / Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq individually no claim. Iran has not acknowledged. The Helsinki-pact architecture (Day 5 of 30, draft expected by 2026-06-15) calls for Saudi-Iran communicative restraint — Saudi non-action over 72 hours is consistent with the Helsinki framework PREVAILING over the 'Saudi territorial breach requires Saudi response' framework. **Saudi was also one of the three Gulf leaders requesting Trump postpone the May 19 strike**, positioning Saudi firmly on the de-escalation side. Yemen's Hadi/PLC-aligned government condemned the drone attack and affirmed 'full solidarity with Riyadh' (YemenMonitor) — cleanest Hadi-government solidarity statement of the cycle, useful as confirmation of the Iraq-militia / Iran-aligned attribution path.

recent_signals.headline: **B1 NEW DRONE LAUNCH VECTOR — 3 DRONES LAUNCHED FROM IRAQI AIRSPACE INTERCEPTED OVER SAUDI AIRSPACE SUNDAY MAY 17 MORNING.** Saudi defense ministry spokesman Brigadier Turki al-Maliki confirmed (CONFIRMED ACTION — Saudi MoD primary; UAE MoFA formal May 18 condemnation; Saudi Gazette, Times of Israel, Asharq Al-Awsat, Middle East Eye independent reporting). First confirmed Saudi territorial breach of cycle. **Iraqi-airspace origin points to Iran-backed Iraqi militia involvement (PMU, Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq most likely vectors by capability and prior pattern — same militias named in WSJ April 21 framing).** No group publicly claimed responsibility through Monday morning IST. Iraqi government has not claimed or disclaimed; Iran-aligned militia public channels (Telegram, Sabereen News) had not posted claim. **The non-claim is itself a signal — operationally consistent with deniable harassment, not declared escalation.** Saudi MoD: 'reserves the right to respond at the appropriate time and place' = ambiguous holding position consistent with Helsinki pact preservation. **New trigger added**: 'Saudi formal kinetic response to May 17 Iraqi-airspace drone launch within 14 days (by 2026-05-31)' at Day 0 of 14. **New edge added**: iraq → saudi-arabia via Iran-aligned-militia proxy channel (2nd-order directness, initial weight 6.0). **Markets cascade**: Brent +2.0% to $111.47 (StanChart $130-145 path activates); USD/INR ₹96.29 record; Sensex/Nifty -1.30%/-1.04%. The Saudi territorial breach is one of the principal drivers per markets dossier C1 chain. **Iraqi southern oil exports remain at force-majeure ~900K bpd vs pre-war 3.3M bpd** — restart contingency unchanged.

recent_signals.headline: NEGATIVE FINDING — no confirmed Kataib Hezbollah, Nujaba or Islamic Resistance in Iraq attack on US forces 17-19 Jul, despite the first American combat deaths of the war. Documented militia attack clusters remain March-April 2026. The physical picture has changed: most US forces are now concentrated in the Kurdistan Region with Ain al-Asad largely vacated, and a **US withdrawal from Iraq is scheduled for September**. Iranian state fire, not militia fire, has been doing the work. Nujaba chief Akram al-Kaabi said on 18 Jul that the resistance is 'determined to expel US forces and companies' — single-sourced to Press TV, RHETORIC only, best read as factional positioning ahead of the September withdrawal and against disarmament. Separately Iraqi oil exports RECOVERED sharply pre-escalation: ~1.5 mb/d via Hormuz and Ceyhan combined in July, roughly three times June volume, though still below pre-war. An unconfirmed secondary claim of July pipeline sabotage could not be corroborated and is NOT carried forward. CONFIRMED (non-attack) / CLAIMED (al-Kaabi).

**The militia firewall HELD — and Baghdad went the other way entirely.** No confirmed Kataib Hezbollah, Nujaba or Islamic Resistance attack on US forces. **The US death in Iraq (18 Jul) was an EOD accident disposing of an Iranian drone, NOT a militia attack** — the distinction is the whole story. An explosive-laden drone was downed near **al-Harir/Erbil** on 20 July — **no attribution, no casualties**, and plausibly Iranian given Iranian drones transit Iraqi airspace daily. Militia output remains propaganda (FPV-drone video) and political criticism of the PM's Washington trip. **AGAINST THE GRAIN: PM al-Zaidi's Washington visit produced 48 agreements with US companies, reported at ~$60 BILLION**, a US commitment to rehabilitate **seven Iraqi banks**, and — strategically — an **Iraq-Syria deal signed IN WASHINGTON to revive the Kirkuk-Baniyas crude pipeline, explicitly to bypass the Strait of Hormuz** and create a Gulf-to-Mediterranean route, which the US publicly hailed. Iraqi oil exports jumped in July. Arabic outlet Noon Post frames the deals as **tied to disarming armed factions** (single Arabic source, REPORTED) — if accurate, that is the Lebanon playbook running on a second front simultaneously. **Al-Zaidi is expected in Tehran ~23 July carrying a US message**, and Iraq's FM says Baghdad is 'ready to mediate between Washington and Tehran.' **The September US withdrawal timetable: NO UPDATE. Treat as unchanged and unverified.** CONFIRMED (non-attack).

**No confirmed militia attack on US forces (firewall holds) — and Baghdad's mediation offer was reportedly REBUFFED.** PM al-Zaidi offered to host US-Iran talks and carry a US message to Tehran; Trump reportedly DECLINED (Al-Hurra), though a competing account has him carrying a message — UNRESOLVED. The National frames Iraq's US economic talks as the 'base to mediate with Iran.' Al-Zaidi's Tehran trip is pending (~23 Jul). No new militia kinetic activity; the September US withdrawal timetable remains without update. CONFIRMED (non-attack) / REPORTED (mediation rebuff).

Militia firewall holds — no confirmed attack on US forces; the one kinetic item was three drones INTERCEPTED near a US consulate in northern Iraq (no impact, no attribution). The al-Zaidi mediation channel is contradictory (Trump 'declined the relay' 21 Jul vs 'asks al-Zaidi to mediate' 22 Jul — UNRESOLVED); ISNA frames his Tehran visit as aiming to keep Baghdad OUT of the conflict. No new on the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline or the September withdrawal timetable. CONFIRMED (non-attack).
